findings.message: Cadence is every 600s (10 min): fine for a demo, unusual for payroll

brief.headline: Creates a 10-minute cadence payroll plan for 3 devs totaling 270 USDC.e per run, funded for 24 runs.
what_changes: Creates a standing order plan titled 'Core team retainer, every 10 minutes' on the standing-order contract.
Sets a cadence of 600 seconds (10 minutes) with no start or end date specified.
Allocates 120 USDC.e to dev1, 90 USDC.e to dev2, and 60 USDC.e to design per run.
Sets a cap of 270 USDC.e per run, matching the sum of individual allocations.
Transfers 6,480 USDC.e from the treasury to fund the plan for 24 runs.
risks: Cadence is every 600s (10 min): fine for a demo, unusual for payroll
No end date is set, meaning the plan will continue indefinitely after the 24 funded runs if not manually stopped (model)
The 10-minute interval is highly irregular for standard payroll, potentially indicating a test or misconfiguration (model)
questions_for_proposer: Is the 10-minute cadence intentional for this payroll plan, or is it a test configuration?
What is the plan for stopping the plan after the 24 funded runs, given no end date is set?
Why is the funding amount exactly sufficient for 24 runs with no buffer for potential failures or adjustments?

checks: signer matches exactly one attested model TEE
